cards.explanation: The answer is False. Agur says, “I have not learned wisdom, and I have no knowledge of the Holy One.” He says it plain, no dressing it up, friends. Then he turns around and talks about God's words being flawless. Humble start, strong finish. (Proverbs 30:3, 5)

The answer is His name and His Son's name. After all those big questions, Agur asks, “What is His name, and what is the name of His Son…” He's asking about the One who gathered the wind and bound up the waters. Then he adds, “…surely you know!” (Proverbs 30:4)

The answer is every word of God. Agur says, “Every word of God is flawless…” Every word, friends, not just the ones I like. I've called my own batches flawless before, and the cookies had opinions. (Proverbs 30:5)
The answer is True. Agur says God “…is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.” A shield only works if you get behind it, bakers. Taking refuge means exactly that. (Proverbs 30:5)

The answer is adding to His words. Agur says, “Do not add to His words, lest He rebuke you and prove you a liar.” If every word of God is flawless, there's nothing to fix. Notice, friends, the warning is about adding, not about learning. (Proverbs 30:5-6)

The answer is to keep lies far from him. Agur asks, “Keep falsehood and deceitful words far from me.” That's his first request. Notice he asks God to keep lies away from him, friends. That's a man who knows he needs help. (Proverbs 30:7-8)

The answer is False. Agur says, “Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread that is my portion.” He doesn't ask for a pile of money or for empty shelves, bakers. He asks for his portion, and that's it. (Proverbs 30:8)

The answer is that he might deny God. Agur says, “…I may have too much and deny You, saying, ‘Who is the LORD?’…” Having plenty could lead him to say that, friends. So he asks for just his portion. (Proverbs 30:9)

The answer is steal. Agur says, “Or I may become poor and steal, profaning the name of my God.” That's the other side of his worry, bakers. Too much and he might deny God, too little and he might steal. So he asks for the bread that is his portion. (Proverbs 30:8-9)

The answer is True. Agur says, “Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will bear the guilt.” Say something false about a servant and it comes back on you, friends. The guilt lands on the one who slandered. (Proverbs 30:10)

The answer is fathers. Agur says, “There is a generation of those who curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers.” It's the first of his four generations, bakers. Fathers and mothers both show up in the line. (Proverbs 30:11)

The answer is False. Agur says, “There is a generation of those who are pure in their own eyes and yet unwashed of their filth.” Pure in their own eyes isn't the same as clean, friends. That's the gap he points out. (Proverbs 30:12)

The answer is the oppressed and the needy. Agur says, “…there is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, devouring the oppressed from the earth and the needy from among men.” It's a hard picture, bakers. The ones being devoured are the oppressed and the needy. (Proverbs 30:14)

The answer is True. Agur says there are three things never satisfied, four that never say ‘Enough!’ Then he lists them: “Sheol, the barren womb, land never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, ‘Enough!’” He starts with three and lists four, friends. (Proverbs 30:15-16)

The answer is may the ravens of the valley pluck it out. Agur says, “…may the ravens of the valley pluck it out and young vultures devour it.” I think this is one of the hardest lines in the chapter, bakers. He's talking about the eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother. (Proverbs 30:17)

The answer is too wonderful for him. Agur says, “There are three things too wonderful for me, four that I cannot understand…” Then he lists the eagle, the snake, the ship and the man with a maiden. For a man who started the chapter saying he's ignorant, friends, he sure notices a lot of wonders. (Proverbs 30:18-19)

The answer is “I have done nothing wrong.” Agur says, “This is the way of an adulteress: She eats and wipes her mouth and says, ‘I have done nothing wrong.’” She says she has done nothing wrong, bakers. It's a serious picture. (Proverbs 30:20)

The answer is a maidservant who takes her mistress's place. Agur's list ends with “…a maidservant who supplants her mistress.” That's the fourth thing the earth cannot bear up under, friends. It comes right after an unloved woman who marries. (Proverbs 30:21-23)

The answer is storing up their food in summer. Agur says, “The ants are creatures of little strength, yet they store up their food in the summer…” Small, but they plan ahead, bakers. Wise little things. (Proverbs 30:25)

The answer is True. Agur says, “…the locusts have no king, yet they all advance in formation…” No king, and they still advance in formation, friends. That's the kind of order I'd love in my kitchen. (Proverbs 30:27)

The answer is in the palaces of kings. Agur says, “…the lizard can be caught in one’s hands, yet it is found in the palaces of kings.” Small enough to catch, and still in the palace, bakers. Fourth on his list of small things that are wise. (Proverbs 30:28)

The answer is False. Agur describes “…a lion, mighty among beasts, refusing to retreat before anything…” It doesn't back down, friends. That's why it makes his list of things stately in their stride. (Proverbs 30:29-30)

The answer is king. Agur finishes the list with “…a king with his army around him.” The lion, the rooster and the he-goat come first, bakers. All four are impressive in their walk. (Proverbs 30:29-31)

The answer is to put your hand over your mouth. Agur says, “If you have foolishly exalted yourself or if you have plotted evil, put your hand over your mouth.” Stop talking, friends. My mustache already covers my mouth, so I'm halfway there. (Proverbs 30:32)

The answer is strife. Agur says, “For as the churning of milk yields butter, and the twisting of the nose draws blood, so the stirring of anger brings forth strife.” Churn milk and you get butter, bakers. Stir anger and you get strife. (Proverbs 30:33)
